display-numeral.purpose: The inspector's carry-over percentage; counts up to its value.

title.purpose: Window title, grid group headings, popover titles.

label.purpose: Sidebar sections, inspector section titles, status pills; sentence case.

materials.name: glass
materials.value: background: var(--glass); backdrop-filter: blur(26px) saturate(185%); border: 1px solid var(--glass-edge); box-shadow: var(--glass-shadow), inset 0 1px 0 var(--glass-hi)
materials.purpose: Liquid Glass for floating controls, bars, popovers, sheets, toasts. Opaque (elevated) under Reduce Transparency.

materials.name: native-vibrancy
materials.value: NSVisualEffectView material .sidebar, blendingMode .behindWindow, behind a transparent WKWebView
materials.purpose: Real behind-window vibrancy under the sidebar in the Mac app (html.native); browser uses sidebar-fill.

materials.name: scroll-edge
materials.value: backdrop-filter: blur(14px) saturate(160%) with a fading content-colour gradient and mask
materials.purpose: Toolbar edge once content scrolls under it.

materials.name: lit
materials.value: radial-gradient(180px circle at pointer, rgba(255,255,255,.16), transparent 70%)
materials.purpose: Pointer-following light on the selection bar and Masks button.

shadows.name: panel-shadow
shadows.purpose: Sidebar and inspector (dark). Light: 0 8px 26px rgba(20,20,50,.09), 0 1px 2px rgba(20,20,50,.08).

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus everywhere; tiles use a 3px ring plus 6px accent-soft halo.

motion.name: spring
motion.purpose: Apple-style spring (~5% overshoot) for presses, chips, popovers, ticks, the view-switch thumb. Deliberate overshoot, pinned by the user.

motion.name: spring-soft
motion.purpose: Larger travel: panel columns, sheets, selection bar arrival, search width, view-transition groups, meter reflow.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Fades in, inspector swap-in, curve draw, number roll.

motion.name: ease-in
motion.purpose: Exits: popover out .16s, sheet out .18s, inspector swap-out .12s, toast out .2s.

motion.name: view-transition-morph
motion.value: group .5s spring-soft; old/new cross-fade .22s; root .18s ease-out
motion.purpose: Grid/List morph: each .tile-face and row swatch carries a view-transition-name and flies to its new place.

motion.name: count-up
motion.value: rAF, ease-out cubic, 520ms first reveal / 360ms between presets, clamped to its range
motion.purpose: Carry-over percentage counts to its value.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: travel off; popovers, sheets and inspector swaps cross-fade (.1-.2s); transitions limited to opacity and colour

narrative.northStar: The Window Apple Would Have Shipped
narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Window Apple Would Have Shipped"**

Partly is one Mac window that reads like Photos or Finder: a floating sidebar of sources and groups, a library browsed as a grid of swatch tiles or a sortable list, an inspector on the right, and a floating glass bar at the bottom that holds the one primary action, Create. It is built from macOS's own materials rather than a web dashboard's boxes: real behind-window vibrancy in the native app, Liquid Glass capsules (blur, saturation, a specular top edge, a soft drop shadow) for everything that floats over content, system colours for meaning, SF Pro for text and SF Pro Rounded for the numbers that matter.

Density is a desktop app's density, not a web page's: 13px body text, 30px controls, 8px insets, a 52px title band shared with the traffic lights. Colour is almost entirely neutral. The system blue marks selection and the primary action; green, orange, purple and gray say how a setting carries over and nothing else. The only rich colour on screen is the presets themselves, each drawn as a computed swatch: a synthetic landscape pushed through that preset's own settings.

Motion is part of the material. Things arrive on springs (about 5% overshoot), leave faster on a plain ease-in, and travel only where travel explains something: the List and Grid morph, the sidebar highlight sliding to the current row, popovers growing from their button, the carry-over meter reflowing between presets, the score counting to its value.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default, light following the system or Settings; every colour token has both variants.
Glass only on things that float: toolbar capsules, selection bar, popovers, sheets, toasts, the sticky list header.
One primary action per screen, in system blue, inside the floating bar.
Every preset is shown as its own computed swatch; every figure is computed from the preset.
Springs in, quick out; Reduce Motion keeps fades and stops all travel.
The same page runs in the native WKWebView window and in a plain browser.

rules.name: The System Colour Rule
rules.body: Every hue is an Apple system colour with its accessible light-appearance variant. No brand colour, no gradients as decoration; the one gradient fill is the welcome screen's drop halo.

rules.name: The Status Means Status Rule
rules.body: Green, orange, purple and gray belong to carry-over status. They never decorate, never mark selection, and always appear with a text label (pill, legend) beside the colour.

rules.name: The Swatches Are the Colour Rule
rules.body: The interface stays neutral so the presets' computed swatches are the richest thing on screen.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change (counts, percentages, setting deltas, tallies) uses tabular figures so values never jitter as they update.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings and labels are sentence case at 11px/650 the way macOS writes them; nothing is set in tracked uppercase.

rules.name: The Glass Floats Rule
rules.body: Glass is for things that float over content. Content itself (tiles, rows, inspector cards) is never glass.

rules.name: The Opaque Fallback Rule
rules.body: Under Reduce Transparency (system setting, or forwarded from macOS as `html.reduce-transparency`) all backdrop filters turn off and glass becomes `elevated`. The design must read fully without blur.

dos: **Do** take every colour from the token set, in both appearances; add a light variant (with an accessible ink) for any new colour.
**Do** use glass (blur 26px + saturate 185%, `glass-edge` hairline, `glass-hi` top edge, `glass-shadow`) only for floating controls, bars, popovers, sheets and toasts.
**Do** use `--spring` / `--spring-soft` (linear() springs with about 5% overshoot, cubic-bezier fallbacks) for arrivals and `--ease-in` at 120-180ms for exits.
**Do** keep fades and stop all travel under Reduce Motion; turn glass opaque under Reduce Transparency; strengthen separators under Increase Contrast.
**Do** show presets as computed swatches from `swatch.js`, and compute every percentage, count and status from the presets themselves.
**Do** keep the page working the same in WKWebView (`html.native`, drag regions, forwarded settings) and in a plain browser.
**Do** draw icons as 24px line drawings at 1.7 stroke in `currentColor`; draw apps as generic objects (a cloud, a display, a camera).
**Do** use tabular figures for every changing number.
donts: **Don't** use Adobe's or Lightroom's logos, lettermarks, colours or branding anywhere; this app is not made by or affiliated with Adobe.
**Don't** show anyone's purchased presets in screenshots or committed assets; samples are synthetic.
**Don't** invent figures, testimonials or counts; a number on screen is computed or it is not shown.
**Don't** imply the app writes to Lightroom's own files; they are read-only.
**Don't** put glass on content (tiles, rows, cards), and don't stack glass on glass.
**Don't** use the status colours for decoration or selection, or show a status by colour alone.
**Don't** set labels in tracked uppercase or add kicker lines above titles.
**Don't** let anything travel or bounce when Reduce Motion is on.
